To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reducing the number number of short intervals (< 11 hours) in a work schedule improves sleep quality and recovery from work.
the reduction of the number of short work shifts improves the recovery from shift work.
a reduced number of intervals between work shifts results in an increase in sleep heart rate variability parameters indicating better physiological recovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the work environment on the recovery of the autonomic regulation of the heart rate during the sleep.
the development and implementation of a shift system that would be more favorable to health and safety of shift workers, as well as the development of new methods for shift system evaluation.
a practical issue of the work organization, which may be used to reduce health risks associated with shift work and improve the working conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a reduced number of intervals between work shifts would be a useful tool to enhance the physiological and psychosocial health of shift workers.
the recovery of the parasympathetically dominated autonomic nervous system during the sleep can be promoted by implementing the ergonomic recommendations for shift work.
reducing the number and/or the duration of the short intervals between work-shifts is an effective way of improving the physiological recovery during sleep.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implementation of the ergonomic recommendations in the shift system can improve the recovery of autonomics nervous system and thus, improve the quality of work and health.
the recovery from shift work can not only be improved by increasing the sleep duration, but also by increasing the time of sleep.
a reduction in the frequency of the short intervals between work-shifts is an effective method to improve the recovery of the autonomic regulation during the sleep.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction of short intervals between shift works is a simple and cost-effective measure to improve the recovery from shift work.
a reduction of the number of short work shifts can be a cost-effective way of improving shift workers’ health and well-being.
the reduction of the number of short work shifts can be used as a practical tool to promote the health of shift workers.
